subject: Post-call: TTFT & streaming requirements - FintechAI
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Samir Shah <samir.shah@fintechai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-02-20T15:12:00-08:00
Subject: Post-call: TTFT & streaming requirements - FintechAI

Hi Samir - thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery + a couple of clarification items so we can size a focused perf run and draft a mutual action plan.

Recap (from what I captured):
- Primary use case: real-time customer support assistants in mobile/web apps (short prompts, 200-600 token responses).
- Critical SLO: time-to-first-token (TTFT) is the biggest UX driver for your team. You said target is ~200ms p95 for typical responses.
- Throughput & concurrency: expecting sustained ~150-250 QPS during peak, with bursts to ~400 QPS; target concurrency per model ~40-60 concurrent streams.
- Streaming: prefer server-sent events (SSE) on mobile with chunk cadence that feels "instant" - you mentioned ~100ms cadence as ideal.
- Security: standard SOC2 / data residency constraints - Elaine (procurement) will handle any docs.

Clarification items / asks:
1) Can you confirm the TTFT p95 target (is 200ms p95 hard, or is 300ms acceptable for an initial pilot)?
2) For streaming cadence: do you need every chunk to be ~100ms or is a 50-200ms range acceptable?
3) Can you share a representative payload (prompt + expected response length) we can use for the perf test?

What we can do next:
- Marissa (cc) can run a quick hosted perf run against an equivalent open model and share measured TTFT + per-chunk latencies.
- We'll produce a short test plan + expected results and then schedule a 1 hour perf review.

I've attached a brief design note (redwood-ttft-design.pdf) with recommended streaming approaches (SSE vs WebSocket) and our default chunking strategy.

Thanks - I can be flexible on timing next week for the perf run.

--Aditya
Aditya Rao
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0198

Attachment: redwood-ttft-design.pdf (1.2MB - design note, charts)

From: Samir Shah <samir.shah@fintechai.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Elaine Ortiz <elaine.ortiz@fintechai.com>
Date: 2026-02-21T09:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: TTFT & streaming requirements - FintechAI

Thanks, Aditya - great write-up and exactly what I was hoping for. Quick answers below: 

- TTFT: 200ms p95 is our aspirational SLA for GA; for the pilot (Q2) we can accept up to 300ms p95 while we tune. So please size for 200ms but call out pilot expectations.
- Throughput/concurrency: confirmed - sustained 200 QPS, concurrent sessions ~50. We do have predictable diurnal spikes up to 400 QPS.
- Streaming cadence: mobile is priority - we'd like chunks to arrive roughly every 80-120ms for a natural typing experience. If that's not achievable at scale with SSE, call it out and propose fallback cadence.

I'll pull together a representative set of prompts and expected response sizes (short 80-200 token responses + some longer 400-600 token flows) and share by end of day tomorrow.

Elaine - tagging you on the thread; procurement timeline is end of month for pilot approvals - can you share any standard docs you need?

--Samir
Samir Shah
Head of Product, FintechAI
samir.shah@fintechai.com

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Shah <samir.shah@fintechai.com>, Elaine Ortiz <elaine.ortiz@fintechai.com>
Date: 2026-02-22T11:40:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: TTFT & streaming requirements - FintechAI

Marissa / Laura - looping you in to help validate sizing and to request a targeted perf run. Samir confirmed targets in his reply (copied below).

Ask: can we run a focused hosted perf test next week with the following config?
- Model: 1-2 representative open models (e.g., Llama2-13B / Mistral small) and one quantized variant.
- Input: 3 prompt templates Samir will provide (short, mid, long).
- Target steady-state: 200 QPS for 10 minutes, with a 1-minute burst to 400 QPS.
- Measurement: TTFT p50/p95/p99, per-chunk latency distribution, CPU/GPU utilization, network RTTs.

I've attached a short test plan (ttft-test-plan.md) - feel free to update with any infra needs. Proposed owners: Marissa to run the bench and share raw csv + summary; Aditya to coordinate scheduling and share results with FintechAI.

Samir - if you can share the prompt set and a test user token (or allow our test runner to use a scoped demo key), we'll get this scheduled.

Thanks -
Aditya

Attachment: ttft-test-plan.md (test steps, metrics to collect)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Samir Shah <samir.shah@fintechai.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-02-24T16:20:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: TTFT & streaming requirements - FintechAI

Hi Samir / Aditya - thanks for the context. Quick tech response and what I'll deliver in the perf run.

Summary (short answers):
- Typical TTFT expectation on our hosted infra: for 512-token responses using an optimized quantized 13B variant we see ~120-180ms p95 under controlled conditions for single-request latency. Under steady 200 QPS (with continuous batching) p95 tends to increase; our goal is to keep p95 <= 200-250ms with appropriate batching/kv-cache policies.
- Streaming & chunk cadence: SSE is perfectly fine for mobile. Recommended cadence to feel "real-time": 50-150ms per chunk on the client (we'll aim for ~80-120ms median cadence in the perf run). Important note: chunk cadence is influenced by model generation speed and network; we provide client-side guidance in redwood-streaming-guide.pdf to smooth UX (adaptive chunk sizes + small token prefills).
- Concurrency/throughput: to meet 200 QPS with p95 ~200ms you'll want a combination of autoscaling headroom and batching config. I'll include suggested Dedicated configurations and an estimate of GPU capacity (vCPU/GPU ratios).

Deliverables for the run I'll execute next Tue/Wed (need Samir's prompt set):
1) Raw CSV with per-request TTFT and per-chunk timestamps (ttft-bench-20260224.csv).
2) Summary: p50/p95/p99 TTFT and chunk-cadence distribution.
3) Short doc with recommended prod settings (batching, kv-cache TTLs, SSE chunk strategy) - attached redwood-streaming-guide.pdf.

Next steps: Samir - if you can drop the prompt set to the shared link (or paste in the next reply) and provide a scoped test key, I'll queue the run and share results within 48 hours of execution. After that, we can schedule a 30-45 minute review to go over tuning and Dedicated sizing.

Thanks -
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com | +1 (650) 555-0112

Attachments: ttft-bench-20260224.csv (raw results), redwood-streaming-guide.pdf (recommendations)
